question: Which statements about subset selection are true? (Select all that apply)

answers.answer: Best subset selection has to evaluate 2^p models
answers.feedback: Correct! Every predictor can be in the model or not.

answers.answer: Backward stepwise selection starts with the full model
answers.feedback: Correct! It then removes one predictor at a time.

answers.answer: Backward stepwise selection is preferred over forward stepwise selection when p > n
answers.feedback: Not quite. Backward selection starts with the full model, which cannot be fitted when p > n.

answers.answer: Forward stepwise selection always finds the same subset as best subset selection
answers.feedback: Not quite. It did here, but a greedy search can miss the best combination.

question: You add one more predictor to a linear regression model. What happens to the R² on the training data?

answers.answer: It increases or stays the same
answers.feedback: Correct! The model can always set the new coefficient to zero, so the fit on the training data cannot get worse. This is why we compare models with cross-validation.
Not quite. That is true for the cross-validated or test R², but not for the training R².
Not quite. Think about what the model could do with a useless predictor: set its coefficient to zero.

question: Why do we still need a separate test set, even though the feature selection already uses cross-validation?

answers.answer: Because the best of many CV scores is too optimistic for the selected model
answers.feedback: Correct! We picked the subset with the highest CV score, so its score is partly luck.

answers.answer: Because cross-validation does not work for linear regression
answers.feedback: Not quite. Cross-validation works for any model.

answers.answer: Because the test set is larger than the CV folds
answers.feedback: Not quite. The size is not the issue. The CV scores were used to choose the model, so they cannot also give an unbiased estimate of its performance.
